newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia cuts internal coffee price.
newsitem.headline: Colombia cuts internal coffee price.

text.p: Colombia cut its internal coffee price by 14,000 pesos per 125-kilo load Thursday in a move the head of the National Coffee Growers' Federation said was painful but necessary to help save the institution that pays growers for their crops from a deepening financial crisis.

With the price cut, effective Friday, Dec. 6, growers who have been paid 235,500 pesos per 125-kilo load since Aug. 21 will now receive 221,500 pesos, said the federation's general manager, Jorge Cardenas.

The price per 125-kilo that has remained in effect since last August, when it was raised from 201,500 pesos, was actually 221,500 pesos. But growers were awarded an additional 14,000 peso premium, paid in the form of a bond instead of cash, because of the poor outlook for coffee in the 1996 calendar year.

Cardenas, who spoke on a final day of a four-day annual meeting of coffee growers in Bogota, said the new price was likely to hold throughout 1997, although he cautioned that more price cuts may be unavoidable.
